pair_verifier.reason: The archived solver reflects only when the diagonal target is a mirror; the native constructor reflects when the cell across the wall axis is a mirror. They differ exactly on endpoint-sensitive scenes (corner contact with a mirror end), so the archived checker rejected every endpoint-sensitive native pair (c75138a constructor: 220/220 endpoint-sensitive pairs in 600 seeded draws; 400/1000 pairs overall with seed 11, see counterexample). This checker replays the side-contact reading with the independent coordinate tracer of beam_endpoint_evidence. Exported programs and the unchanged colour-evidence gate still require demonstrations to determine the convention.

draft_notes.author: Claude CLI four-reading proposal, host strict inference and independent replay
draft_notes.explanation: Trace the diagonal beam in visible coordinates. Determine parallel wall axis from mirror/glass line geometry. Candidate endpoint conventions are side contact (native constructor), either side or diagonal contact, diagonal-target contact with local corner reflection, and diagonal-target contact reflecting across the wall axis. A candidate must reproduce every demo output and each visible beam-prefix bend, including the query prefix. Return only if surviving candidates agree on the complete query grid. No no-survivor, documented-rule or axis fallback.
draft_notes.limitations: Four explicit candidate conventions, not a proof that every imaginable rule is excluded. The native side-contact rule can overwrite a mirror endpoint (piercing) or reflect beside its end (grazing). We preserve and label that behavior; physical terminology alone does not prove the intended endpoint convention. Three demonstrations may be insufficient, requiring informative-context resampling while preserving the query. Input must show a diagonal monotone beam chain from a unique border tail and parallel walls.
draft_notes.diagnosis: The native constructor is deterministic. The dispute is between plausible endpoint interpretations compatible with weak demonstrations, not two labels emitted by identical native calls. The v3 suggestion to reject pierces/grazes in the generator was not applied. A direct source should learn the endpoint reading from visible examples rather than hardcode a documented interpretation or use a D4-selected convention.

host_review.source_changes: Require nonempty well-formed demonstrations, valid visible chain and unambiguous wall axis. Remove arbitrary rule fallback, no-survivor reset and malformed-demo skipping. All query-incompatible prefix hypotheses are eliminated by input evidence only.
host_review.independence: Gate uses coordinate dictionaries, orders the monotone prefix along the wall axis, determines its border tail, and replays the whole trajectory. Emitted target traverses a diagonal-neighbour graph and extends both visible endpoints with NumPy grid operations.
host_review.tests: Seven tests: weak-context rejection of pierce/graze; informative native demo preserves both; visible query-prefix bend disambiguates weak context; counterfactual demonstrated endpoint rule changes output; independent predictions agree across D4; all original fixtures; absent/invalid demos reject. Query labels may be omitted or poisoned without changing admission.
